## Broadcasting
As outlined before loops can be used to iterate through a vector and perform defined operations for each individual element. If we want to sum up two vectors elementwise we could use a `for` loop:
```{julia}
x = [1.0,2.0,3.0]
y = [4.0,5.0,6.0]
z = zeros(length(x))

for i in eachindex(x)
    z[i] = x[i] + y[i]
end

display(z)
```
The same action can be written in a shorter way. In this notation the `.` operator is used - this is called broadcasting:
```{julia}
z .= x .+ y

display(z)
```
It is also possible to use the `@.` macro
```{julia}
@. z = x + y

display(z)
```
Functions can also be broadcasted to apply them on all eleemnts of an array:
```{julia}
x = [1.0,2.0,3.0]
z = zeros(length(x))

z = exp.(x)

display(z)
```
## Try it on Your Own
Create a LinRange with 100 points ranging from 0 to 2$\pi$ and store it in the variable x, then compute the sine and the cosine of the LinRange using the `sin()` and `cos()` function with the `.` operator and store them in the variables sin_x and cos_x. To visualize use this little skript:
```julia
using Plots
p = plot(x, sin_x)
    plot!(x,cos_x)
display(p)
```
